The wiki article stipulates that the Kuiper belt is somewhere between 20-200 times the mass of the asteroid belt, not 200 times as large. Pluto and Eris, the two largest Kuiper belt objects, have a combined mass greater than 20 times the mass of the asteroid belt.

So yes, two dwarf planets and a dozen or so other dwarf planets do make something 20-200 times the mass of the asteroid belt.

And these are just the object we know about. Keep in mind finding stuff in the Kuiper belt is extremely difficult. It's all fairly fall from us, it's all fairly small, it's all fairly far from the sun, and it all moves fairly slowly. It's easy to get these objects mixed up with distant stars.
